exact_identity: Indifi Technologies Pvt. Ltd. — Indian fintech lender focused on unsecured MSME lending. Dataset referenced in NBER Working Paper w34148 (Gopal et al., 'FinTech Lending and Cashless Payments').
availability_method: Proprietary dataset shared with academic researchers under a data-use agreement. Not publicly downloadable. Must be obtained via direct research partnership with Indifi.
lawful_borrower_level_access: Yes — borrower/loan-level records are lawfully accessible by Indifi as the originating lender. External researchers access only under a signed data-use agreement with pseudonymization.
features_at_prediction_time: Complete applicant information set gathered at screening: applicant demographics, business characteristics, 6-month payment-transaction history (digital payments flowing through the business), and merged credit-bureau scores. All point-in-time at application.
subsequent_repayment_labels: Yes — loan performance/outcomes as of 2022. Financing outcomes (approved/declined) and loan repayment performance (default/non-default).
label_definition_window_maturity: Default defined by lender. Loan-level outcome observed over the loan's tenure; data as of 2022 provides mature follow-up for loans originated 2015-2022.
license_consent_restrictions: Governed by Indifi's internal data policy and a researcher data-use agreement. Not open-licensed. Redistribution prohibited. Personal data protected under Indian privacy law. Requires Indifi legal/compliance sign-off.
acquisition_effort_blockers: High — requires establishing a research relationship with Indifi, signing a DUA, and agreeing to pseudonymization, purpose limitation, and publication review. Indifi has previously shared data with academic researchers (evidence of willingness).
verification_status: Verified (referenced in peer-reviewed NBER working paper; dataset characteristics described in paper)
indian_nbfc_relevance: High — Indian MSME unsecured loans; directly relevant to NBFC underwriting. Payment-history features align with AA-based cashflow underwriting.
notes: Strongest evidence that an Indian lender possesses labeled borrower-level data and is willing to share for research. Best single lead for a data partnership. Not a public dataset.

exact_identity: An unnamed Indian microfinance institution. Dataset referenced in SMJ paper 'Community influence on microfinance loan defaults under crisis conditions: Evidence from Indian demonetization' (doi:10.1002/smj.3558).
availability_method: Proprietary dataset shared with academic researchers under a data-use agreement. Firm identity not disclosed in paper.
lawful_borrower_level_access: Yes — borrower-level records accessible by the partner MFI. Researchers access under DUA.
features_at_prediction_time: Borrower demographics and loan characteristics as recorded in the firm's database at origination. Point-in-time application features.
subsequent_repayment_labels: Yes — full repayment records from July 2016 to February 2017 for 2,036,108 borrowers with active loans at demonetization (Nov 8 2016).
label_definition_window_maturity: Default/repayment observed over Jul 2016–Feb 2017. Repayment records are actual ledger data. Crisis-period window (demonetization shock).
license_consent_restrictions: Governed by the partner MFI's data policy and researcher DUA. Firm identity confidential. Not open-licensed.
acquisition_effort_blockers: High — requires identifying and partnering with an Indian MFI willing to share anonymized repayment data. The paper proves such MFIs exist and share data, but the specific firm is unnamed.
verification_status: Verified (referenced in peer-reviewed SMJ article; 2,036,108 borrowers described)
indian_nbfc_relevance: Medium-High — Indian MFI group-lending context; relevant for microcredit NBFCs but group-liability dynamics differ from individual NBFC personal loans.
notes: Proves Indian MFIs share borrower-level repayment data with researchers. Specific partner must be identified independently. Larger sample (2M borrowers) but crisis-period window limits generality.

exact_identity: Reserve Bank of India, Central Repository of Information on Large Credits (CRILC). Published via RTI response (App. no RBIND/R/E/22/02061). Hosted on dataful.in.
lawful_borrower_level_access: Yes — borrower-level records (corporate borrowers). Individual retail borrowers NOT included (threshold ₹25 lakh+).
features_at_prediction_time: bank_name, borrower_name, value (amount owed in ₹ crore), data_as_on, units, notes. No application-time features. No financial ratios, income, or bureau data.
subsequent_repayment_labels: Yes — wilful defaulter classification and amount owed. But this is a list of DEFAULTERS ONLY (no non-defaulter comparison group).
label_definition_window_maturity: Wilful defaulter classification per RBI norms (dues ≥ ₹25 lakh). Single snapshot as of Dec 31 2021. No outcome horizon or maturity window (these are already-classified defaulters).
license_consent_restrictions: RBI CRILC data released via RTI. dataful.in republishes under their terms. Check RBI reuse and dataful.in terms. Borrower names are public (defaulter list), so this is not personal-data protected, but it is corporate-only.
acquisition_effort_blockers: Low — publicly downloadable. But: corporate-only, defaulters-only (no negatives), no features. Cannot train a default-risk model from this alone.
verification_status: Verified (3057 rows, 6 columns; data schema and preview confirmed on dataful.in)
indian_nbfc_relevance: Low — corporate large-borrower defaulters only; no retail/NBFC personal loan relevance; no features; no non-defaulter group.
notes: Useful as supplementary public evidence of Indian default prevalence at the corporate level. NOT a training dataset for retail NBFC underwriting.

exact_identity: RBI DBIE (Database on Indian Economy) and NPCI monthly product statistics. Locally held copies in Data/india_banking and Data/india_upi.
availability_method: Publicly downloadable from RBI DBIE portal and NPCI. 11 NPCI files + 3 RBI files (1 corrupted) already in workspace.
lawful_borrower_level_access: No — aggregate sectoral/national data only. No borrower-level records.
features_at_prediction_time: Monthly/annual aggregate series: UPI volume/value/banks, sectoral bank credit deployment, industry-wise credit. No applicant features.
subsequent_repayment_labels: No — no repayment or default labels. Aggregate GNPA ratios may be derivable from RBI FSR but not at borrower level.
license_consent_restrictions: RBI and NPCI public statistics. Verify specific reuse terms before redistribution. No personal data.
acquisition_effort_blockers: Very Low — already held locally but aggregate-only. Cannot support borrower-level ML.
verification_status: Verified (local files inspected; 126 NPCI monthly rows + RBI sectoral series)
indian_nbfc_relevance: Low — macro context only. Useful for market sizing and as external covariates but cannot train or validate a borrower default model.
notes: Already in workspace. Macro context only, as documented in Phase 2 data feasibility report.

exact_identity: RBI Master Direction on NBFC-Account Aggregators, 2016. Licensed NBFC-AAs (e.g., CAMSFinServ, NESL, FinVu, Cookiejar, OneMoney). Data flows from FIPs (banks, NBFCs, mutual funds, insurers) to FIUs (lenders) via AA consent artefacts.
availability_method: Consent-based: borrower explicitly consents via a standardized consent artefact specifying data type, purpose, recipient, and duration. Data flows end-to-end encrypted.
lawful_borrower_level_access: Yes — borrower-level financial data accessible with explicit, granular, revocable borrower consent. AA is data-blind (cannot see content). FIU (lender) receives decrypted data.
features_at_prediction_time: Bank account transactions, balances, statement data, and potentially other financial information (as consented). Point-in-time at consent. AA does NOT provide application-form features (income, employment) unless those are in the FIP data.
subsequent_repayment_labels: No — AA provides point-in-time financial data (account aggregations/transactions), NOT subsequent repayment outcomes. Outcomes must come from the lender's own loan performance data.
label_definition_window_maturity: N/A for AA itself. AA is a data-transport mechanism, not a labeled dataset.
license_consent_restrictions: RBI Master Direction on NBFC-Account Aggregators, 2016. Consent artefact is mandatory. Data Protection Act 2023 applies. FIU must be a regulated entity (lender). End-to-end encryption. No data to AA.
acquisition_effort_blockers: Medium — requires the startup to become (or partner with) an FIU, integrate with an AA, and obtain borrower consent for each data pull. Does NOT solve the label problem.
verification_status: Verified (RBI Master Direction; operational AA ecosystem with licensed AAs and live FIPs/FIUs)
indian_nbfc_relevance: High — AA is the lawful, scalable route for consented borrower financial features in India. But it provides features only; labels must come from a lender partnership.
notes: AA solves the feature-acquisition legality problem but not the label problem. Must be combined with a lender data partnership for outcomes. Essential infrastructure for any production Indian credit model.

features_at_prediction_time: Four RBI-licensed Credit Information Companies: TransUnion CIBIL, Equifax India, Experian India, CRIF High Mark.
subsequent_repayment_labels: API access. Requires the requester to be a member/regulated entity (lender) or have a lender partnership. Not publicly accessible.
label_definition_window_maturity: Yes — borrower-level credit data accessible by member lenders under the Credit Information Companies Regulation Act, 2005. Access requires permissible purpose and borrower consent.
license_consent_restrictions: Credit score, account-level trade lines (outstanding balances, payment history, DPD), enquiry records, and bureau-derived attributes. Point-in-time at pull.
acquisition_effort_blockers: Yes — historical payment/DPD history across all lenders is available. However, bureau data is shared across lenders; using it to predict the SAME loan's default risks temporal leakage if not carefully windowed. Future repayment on the subject loan is NOT in the bureau at application time.
verification_status: DPD (days past due) history and account status. Window is the borrower's historical credit file. Subject-loan outcome is not observable at application.
indian_nbfc_relevance: CIC Regulation Act 2005. Member-only access. Permissible-purpose requirement. Borrower consent mandatory. Usage restrictions per CIC agreements.
feasibility_rank: High — requires lender membership or a lender partner to pull bureau data. Not available to a standalone startup without a lending license or partner.
notes: Verified (four RBI-licensed CICs; API marketplaces and aggregators documented)
column16: High — bureau data is the standard feature source for Indian credit underwriting. But access requires a lender relationship. Historical DPD can serve as a label proxy ONLY for loans already on the bureau (not for new-to-credit).
column18: Bureau data is the gold-standard feature source. Access is gated behind lender membership. Historical payment data could provide labels for existing borrowers but introduces selection bias (only approved borrowers appear). New-to-credit borrowers have no bureau history.

exact_identity: Kaggle dataset 'Credit Risk with Home Loans' by Gauri Verma. 5000 synthetic records.
availability_method: Publicly downloadable from Kaggle. CC0 Public Domain license.
lawful_borrower_level_access: No — synthetic data, not real borrower records.
features_at_prediction_time: loan_id, applicant_income, loan_amount, loan_term, credit_score, employment_years, property_value, ltv_ratio, dti_ratio, loan_purpose, loan_status, default_flag.
subsequent_repayment_labels: Yes — default_flag (binary), but SYNTHETIC labels, not observed outcomes.
label_definition_window_maturity: Synthetic. No real observation window. Labels are generated, not observed.
license_consent_restrictions: CC0 Public Domain. Free to use.
acquisition_effort_blockers: Very Low — freely downloadable. But synthetic labels are not evidence of real repayment behavior.
verification_status: Verified (Kaggle page inspected: explicitly states '5,000 synthetic records')
indian_nbfc_relevance: Very Low — synthetic. Cannot validate model on Indian borrowers. Useful only for pipeline testing (already have internal synthetic data).
notes: Explicitly synthetic. Not a source of real Indian repayment outcomes. Do not use as evidence of data availability.

exact_identity: Kaggle 'Home Credit Default Risk' competition dataset. Home Credit (international consumer finance lender).
availability_method: Publicly downloadable from Kaggle. Competition license.
lawful_borrower_level_access: Yes — borrower-level records from Home Credit (international, not Indian).
features_at_prediction_time: Application features, bureau data, previous loans, credit card, point-of-sale loans.
subsequent_repayment_labels: Yes — TARGET: client with payment difficulties (late payment > X days on at least one of first Y installments).
label_definition_window_maturity: Default = payment difficulties on early installments. Observation window per loan.
license_consent_restrictions: Kaggle competition license. Home Credit data. Not Indian.
acquisition_effort_blockers: Low — publicly downloadable. But not Indian population.
indian_nbfc_relevance: Medium — methodology benchmark (like LendingClub/UCI), but not Indian validation.
notes: International benchmark. Useful for pipeline methodology, not Indian validation. Already have LendingClub and UCI as benchmarks.

source_name: FACE (Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment) reports
exact_identity: FACE fintech personal loan reports (Apr 2018–Q1 FY2026-27). Drawn from CRIF High Mark records covering 110+ digital NBFCs.
availability_method: Publicly downloadable PDF reports from FACE.
features_at_prediction_time: Aggregate: sanction volume/value, average ticket size, NPA/delinquency rates by segment. No individual borrower features.
subsequent_repayment_labels: Partial — aggregate delinquency rates (e.g., fintech small-ticket personal loan 90-170 DPD = 6.4% as of Mar 2026). Not borrower-level labels.
label_definition_window_maturity: Aggregate delinquency statistics. Not per-loan labels.
license_consent_restrictions: Public reports. CRIF High Mark is the underlying data source but aggregate only.
acquisition_effort_blockers: Low — freely available reports. But aggregate-only.
verification_status: Verified (FACE reports publicly available; statistics cited)
indian_nbfc_relevance: Medium — provides market-level default rates for Indian digital NBFCs, useful for calibration targets and prevalence benchmarks. Not a training dataset.
notes: Useful for understanding Indian fintech default prevalence and setting model evaluation baselines. Not borrower-level training data.

lawful_borrower_level_access: RBI-registered P2P NBFCs: Faircent, LenDenClub, IndiaP2P, Lendbox. Publicly report aggregate NPA rates.
features_at_prediction_time: Platforms publish monthly factsheets with aggregate NPA. Borrower-level loan data would require a data partnership or (for lenders on the platform) portfolio-level data.
subsequent_repayment_labels: Potentially yes — P2P platforms have borrower-level loan and repayment data. Publicly only aggregate NPA is available.
label_definition_window_maturity: Platforms collect borrower application data and repayment history. Exact feature set varies by platform.
license_consent_restrictions: Yes — platforms track loan repayment and NPA at loan level. But not publicly accessible at borrower level.
acquisition_effort_blockers: NPA defined per platform (typically 90+ DPD). Loan-level outcomes tracked internally.
verification_status: RBI P2P NBFC regulations. Borrower data protected. Public aggregate factsheets only.
indian_nbfc_relevance: Medium-High — would require a data partnership with a P2P platform. Some platforms may be open to research collaborations. Public NPA data is aggregate only.
feasibility_rank: Lead (aggregate NPA verified; borrower-level access not yet confirmed)
notes: Medium-High — P2P personal loans are close to NBFC personal loan underwriting. Platforms have labeled data. But borrower-level access requires partnership.
column17: P2P platforms are a promising partnership target for retail personal loan labeled data. Public factsheets confirm they track NPA. Borrower-level access unconfirmed.
